_source: Git-tracked fallback for curia-suggestion-review's 'genuinely uncertain, ask a human' path. Added 2026-09-04, at explicit user request, after diagnosing the real reason Curia Command's live db (the intended destination — see that tab's own 'How an agent flags something uncertain here' panel) was staying empty: writing to the Artifact tool's db from this job's actual execution environment (a headless RemoteTrigger cloud session) triggers an interactive permission prompt ('Claude wants to edit this artifact's data') that nobody is present to answer — confirmed directly from a real run's session log (get_run_log on session_01KQaCpzGQfZsQASZNnSfDWK, 2026-09-04), not guessed. Reading Curia Command's db works fine unattended (read_db never prompts); only writes are blocked. Git writes (this file) already work perfectly reliably for this job — every venue/district promotion has always gone through git — so uncertain items land here instead, and get synced into Curia Command's real Pending Review tab by a human (or an interactive Claude Code session, which doesn't hit the same wall) during a normal check-in. Once synced, an entry's `syncedToPortal` flips to true; the agent should skip re-syncing (but still re-check `status`) on later runs.

Left pending in docs/data/venue-suggestions.json rather than rejected, since today it still technically passes the site-count bar.
